name: Alias-based conditional (selective alias pattern) vs struct-based std::conditional (boostcon/cppnow_presentations_2017, book technique)
listed_description: Alias-based conditional_t is faster to compile than the struct-based conditional because it avoids instantiating new specializations (Odin Holmes' CppNow 2017 talk).
reason: Repo carries only slide code snippets (slides 'Classic conditional', 'Classic conditional cost', 'Selective alias pattern', 'Replace if') in the 29-page PDF 05-17-2017_wednesday/type_based_template_metaprogramming_is_not_dead__odin_holmes__cppnow_05-17-2017.pdf; no compile-time numbers, compiler, flags or benchmark code anywhere in the repo, and the repo has no source tree or license. Slides show the pattern but give no measurement against std::conditional. Directional claim only.
